new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (title 'Mobile Language Team | Nukunu Lesson 2', canonicalhttps://portal.mobilelanguageteam.com.au/lessons/nukunu-lesson-2/). At the end of the lesson, after the consonant list (y.. yuri 'ear'), the section headed 'Some other tips on pronunciation' reads exactly: 'Most Nukunu words carry the stress on the first syllable of the word. The ‘stressed’ part of the word is in bold in these examples:' followed by three table rows with the first syllable in <strong>: **wa**karra 'back of neck', **nga**tyu 'my', **ma**ṛa 'hand'. the compiler quote is verbatim for the sentences; the only differences are formatting (the heading is rendered with a trailing period and the three table rows are run…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the first syllable of the word (bold in the source on wa-karra, nga-tyu, ma-ṛa).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned. (For comparison, Hercus 1999:35 gives Wirangu, a neighbouring Thura-Yura language, initial stress 'as is the case in all the surrounding languages' with secondary stress on the third syllable of longer words; and Eira 2010:39 cites Hercus 1992 as supporting first-syllable stress in related languages.)
new_statements.exceptions: 'Most' words — implies unspecified exceptions; none listed.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level; illustrated with isolated citation forms (nouns/pronouns). Community language-learning lesson in the modern Nukunu orthography, built on Hercus 1992 (the companion wordlist page says its words come from that dictionary).
new_statements.identity_note: Nukunu = Nugunu (Australia), glottocode nugu1241, ISO nnv; Thura-Yura, Pama-Nyungan; southern Flinders Ranges / Port Augusta, SA. The MLT lesson describes the revived modern Nukunu variety (orthography of the Nukunu Wapma Thura / Mobile Language Team programme) built on Hercus 1992's salvage record; same languoid, no dialect distinction. Not to be confused with Nugunu (Cameroon), nugu1242. Note that the Glottolog descriptive reference attached to nugu1241 in our our source list extract (Sun 2015, Sastod Rgyalrong) is a mismatch; Glottolog's actual meds are Hercus 1992 (51 pp.), Black 1917 and Valentine 1886.
